{{Short description|18 mathematical problems stated in 1998}}
'''Smale's problems''' is a list of eighteen [[unsolved problems in mathematics]] proposed by [[Stephen Smale|Steve Smale]] in 1998<ref>{{cite journal | first = Steve | last = Smale|title = Mathematical Problems for the Next Century|journal = Mathematical Intelligencer|year =1998|volume=20|number=2|pages=7–15|doi=10.1007/bf03025291| s2cid = 1331144}}</ref> and republished in 1999.<ref>{{cite book | first = Steve | last = Smale |editor1-first = V. I. | editor1-last = Arnold | editor2-first = M. | editor2-last = Atiyah | editor3-first = P. | editor3-last = Lax | editor4-first = B. | editor4-last = Mazur |editor-link=Vladimir Arnold |editor2-link=Michael Atiyah |editor3-link=Peter Lax |editor4-link=Barry Mazur | title=Mathematics: frontiers and perspectives |publisher=American Mathematical Society|year=1999|pages=271–294 |chapter=Mathematical problems for the next century|isbn=978-0-8218-2070-4}}</ref> Smale composed this list in reply to a request from [[Vladimir Arnold]], then vice-president of the [[International Mathematical Union]], who asked several mathematicians to propose a list of problems for the 21st century. Arnold's inspiration came from the list of [[Hilbert's problems]] that had been published at the beginning of the 20th century.

In his original article Smale written that he chosen the problems using three criteria: simple statement that is preferably precise, personal acquaintance with the problem and belief that solution (or just partial results) for the problem would have great importance for development of mathematics in 21st century.

The four problems from Smale's list: Riemann hypothesis, Poincaré conjecture, P versus NP problem and Navier-Stokes smoothness and existence problem were later put on list of seven [[Millennium Prize problems]] by [[Clay Institute]].

| | 1st
| [[Riemann hypothesis]]: The [[complex number|real part]] of every non-trivial [[zero of a function|zero]] of the [[Riemann zeta function]] is 1/2. (see also [[Hilbert's eighth problem]])
| {{no|{{sort|3|}}Unresolved.}}
| –

| 2nd
| [[Poincaré conjecture]]: Every [[simply connected]], closed 3-[[manifold]] is [[homeomorphic]] to the [[3-sphere]].
| {{yes|{{sort|1|}}Resolved. Result: Yes, follows from [[Thurston's geometrization conjecture]] proved by [[Grigori Perelman]] using [[Ricci flow]].<ref>{{cite arXiv | last = Perelman | first = Grigori | author-link = Grigori Perelman | title = The entropy formula for the Ricci flow and its geometric applications | eprint = math.DG/0211159 | year = 2002 }}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv | last = Perelman | first = Grigori | title = Ricci flow with surgery on three-manifolds | eprint = math.DG/0303109 | year = 2003 }}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv | last = Perelman | first = Grigori | title = Finite extinction time for the solutions to the Ricci flow on certain three-manifolds | eprint = math.DG/0307245 | year = 2003 }}</ref> }}
| 2003

| 3rd
|[[P versus NP problem]]: For all problems for which an [[algorithm]] can ''verify'' a given solution in [[polynomial time]], can an algorithm also ''find'' that solution in polynomial time?
| {{no|{{sort|3|}}Unresolved.}}
| –

| 4th
| [[Shub–Smale tau-conjecture]]:<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Shub | first1=Michael | last2=Smale | first2=Steve | title=On the intractability of Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and an algebraic version of "NP≠P?" | zbl=0882.03040 | journal=Duke Math. J. | volume=81 | pages=47–54 | year=1995 | doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-95-08105-8 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Bürgisser | first1=Peter | title=Completeness and reduction in algebraic complexity theory | zbl=0948.68082 | series=Algorithms and Computation in Mathematics | volume=7 | location=Berlin | publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] | year=2000 | isbn=978-3-540-66752-0 | page=141 }}</ref> let <math>f\in \mathbb{Z}[x]</math> and by <math>\tau(f)</math> denote the minimal number of steps required to generate <math>f</math> using addition, subtraction or multiplication from <math>1</math> and <math>x</math>.

Is there a constant <math>c</math> independent on <math>f</math> such that number of integer zeros of <math>f</math> is bounded by <math>\tau(f)^c</math>?
| {{no|{{sort|3|}}Unresolved.}}
| –

| 5th
| Can one decide if a [[Diophantine equation]] ''ƒ''(''x'',&thinsp;''y'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;0 (input ''ƒ''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;<math display="inline">\mathbb{Z}</math> [''u'',&thinsp;''v'']) has an integer solution, (''x'',&thinsp;''y''), in time (2<sup>''s''</sup>)<sup>''c''</sup> for some universal constant&nbsp;''c''? That is, can the problem be decided in [[exponential time]]?
| {{no|{{sort|3|}}Unresolved.}}
| –

| 6th
| Is the number of relative equilibria ([[central configuration]]s) finite in the [[n-body problem|''n''-body problem]] of [[celestial mechanics]], for any choice of positive [[real number]]s ''m''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''m''<sub>''n''</sub> as the masses?
| {{no|{{sort|3|}}Unresolved. Partial results include proof for almost all systems of five bodies by A. Albouy and V. Kaloshin.<ref>{{cite journal | first1 = A. | last1 = Albouy | first2 = V. | last2 = Kaloshin |title= Finiteness of central configurations of five bodies in the plane |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume= 176 |year=2012 |pages=535–588 |doi=10.4007/annals.2012.176.1.10|doi-access= free }}</ref>}}
| –

| 7th
| Algorithm for finding set of <math>(x_1,...,x_N)</math> such that the [[function (mathematics)|function]]: <math>V_N(x) = \sum_{1 \leq i < j \leq N} \log \frac{1}{\|x_i - x_j\|}</math> is minimized for a distribution of ''N'' points on a [[2-sphere]]. This is related to the [[Thomson problem]].
| {{no|{{sort|3|}}Unresolved.}}
| –

| 8th
| Develop dynamical [[mathematical model]] of market equilibrium to include price adjustments. The [[excess demand]] function in such model is required to satisfy economic-justified conditions:
*be independent on equal inflation of all prices
*satisfy [[Walras's law]]
*return positive demand on free goods
The model may incorporate other economic variables along with the prices but it should be compatible with existing [[general equilibrium theory]].

| {{partial|{{sort|3|}}Gjerstad (2013)<ref>{{cite journal | first = Steven | last = Gjerstad |title= Price Dynamics in an Exchange Economy  | journal=Economic Theory |volume= 52 |issue=2 |year=2013 |pages=461–500|doi=10.1007/s00199-011-0651-5| s2cid = 15322190 }}</ref> extends the deterministic model of price adjustment by Hahn and Negishi (1962)<ref>{{cite journal | first = Frank | last = Hahn |title= A theorem on non-tatonnement stability  | journal=Econometrica |volume= 30 |year=1962 | issue = 3 |pages=463–469| doi = 10.2307/1909889 | jstor = 1909889 }}</ref> to a [[:Category:Stochastic_models|stochastic model]] and shows that when the stochastic model is linearized around the equilibrium the result is the autoregressive price adjustment model used in applied econometrics. He then tests the model with price adjustment data from a general equilibrium experiment.  The model performs well in a general equilibrium experiment with two commodities. Lindgren (2022)<ref>{{cite journal | first = Jussi | last = Lindgren |title = General Equilibrium with Price Adjustments—A Dynamic Programming Approach| journal=Analytics |volume= 1 |issue=1 |year=2022 |pages=27–34|doi=10.3390/analytics1010003 |doi-access=free }}</ref> provides a dynamic programming model for general equilibrium with price adjustments, where price dynamics are given by a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman partial differerential equation. Good Lyapunov stability conditions are provided as well.}}
| 2013, 2022?

| rowspan=2 |11th
| rowspan=2 | Is one-dimensional dynamics generally hyperbolic?<br /><br />(a) Can a [[complex number|complex]] polynomial {{math|''T''}} be approximated by one of the same [[degree of a polynomial|degree]] with the property that every critical point tends to a periodic sink under iteration?<br /><br />(b) Can a smooth map {{math|''T''&nbsp;:&nbsp;[0,1]&nbsp;→&nbsp;[0,1]}} be {{math|''C''<sup>{{hairsp}}''r''</sup>}} approximated by one which is hyperbolic, for all {{math|''r''&nbsp;>&nbsp;1}}?
| {{no|{{sort|3|}}(a) Unresolved, even in the simplest parameter space of polynomials, like the [[Mandelbrot set]].}}
| –
|-
| {{yes|{{sort|2|}}(b) Resolved. Proved by Kozlovski, Shen and van Strien.<ref>{{cite journal | first1 = O. | last1 = Kozlovski | first2 = W. | last2 = Shen | first3 = S. | last3 = van Strien |title= Density of hyperbolicity in dimension one|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume= 166 |year=2007 |pages=145–182 |doi=10.4007/annals.2007.166.145|doi-access= free }}</ref>}}
| 2007

| 12th
| For a [[closed manifold]] <math>M</math> and any <math>r \geq 1</math> let <math>\mathrm{Diff}^r(M)</math> be the [[topological group]] of <math>C^r</math> [[diffeomorphism]]s of <math>M</math> onto itself. Given arbitrary <math>A \in \mathrm{Diff}^r(M)</math>, is it possible to approximate it arbitrary well by such <math> T \in \mathrm{Diff}^r(M)</math> that it commutes only with its iterates?
In other words, is the subset of all diffeomorphisms whose [[Centralizer and normalizer|centralizers]] are trivial dense in <math>\mathrm{Diff}^r(M)</math>?
| {{no|{{sort|3|}}Unresolved. Partial results include proof for {{math|''C''<sup>1</sup>}} [[topological space|topology]] by Christian Bonatti, Sylvain Crovisier and [[Amie Wilkinson]]<ref>{{cite journal | first1 = C. | last1 = Bonatti | first2 = S. | last2 = Crovisier | first3 = A. | last3 = Wilkinson |title= The C<sup>1</sup>-generic diffeomorphism has trivial centralizer |journal=[[Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS]] |volume= 109 |year=2009 |pages=185–244 |doi=10.1007/s10240-009-0021-z|arxiv=0804.1416 | s2cid = 16212782 }}</ref>. Still open in the {{math|''C''<sup>{{hairsp}}''r''</sup>}} topology for {{math|''r''&nbsp;>&nbsp;1}}.}}
| –

| 13th
| [[Hilbert's sixteenth problem|Hilbert's 16th problem]]: Describe relative positions of ovals originating from a [[real number|real]] [[algebraic curve]] and as [[Limit cycle|limit cycles]] of a polynomial [[vector field]] on the plane.
| {{no|{{sort|3|}}Unresolved. Exact description of position of components for real algebraic curves is an open problem, even for small degrees like&nbsp;8. For polynomial vector fields, partial results include proof that they have finitely many limit cycles, but no effective bound is known.}}
| –
|-
| 14th
| Do the properties of the [[Lorenz attractor]] exhibit that of a strange attractor?
| {{yes|{{sort|1|}}Resolved. Result: Yes, solved by [[Warwick Tucker]] using a [[computer-assisted proof]] combined with normal form techniques.<ref>{{cite journal | first = Warwick | last = Tucker |title=A Rigorous ODE Solver and Smale's 14th Problem |journal=Foundations of Computational Mathematics |volume=2 |issue=1 |year=2002 |pages=53–117 |doi=10.1007/s002080010018 |url=https://www.math.cornell.edu/~warwick/main/rodes/JFoCM.pdf| s2cid = 353254 }}</ref>}}
| 2002
|-
| 15th
| Do the [[Navier–Stokes equations]] for [[incompressible flow]] and constant, non-zero [[viscosity]] in <math>\mathbb{R}^3</math> always have a [[Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness|unique smooth solution]] that extends for all time?
| {{no|{{sort|1|}} On 8 September 2026, OpenAI published an anonymized paper with a proposed solution to this problem, claiming to prove finite-time breakdown for the forced three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations on <math>\mathbb{R}^3</math>.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-06 |title=On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem |url=https://openai.com/index/navier-stokes-solution/ |access-date=2026-09-09 |website=OpenAI |language=en-US}}</ref> The proof wasn't published in any peer-review source and has not passed independent review yet.
}}
| –

| 16th
| [[Jacobian conjecture]]: If ''F''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''k<sup>N</sup>''&nbsp;→&nbsp;''k<sup>N</sup>'' is [[Regular map (algebraic geometry)|regular mapping]] and the [[Jacobian matrix and determinant|Jacobian determinant]] of ''F'' is a non-zero constant and ''k'' has [[Characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] 0, then ''F'' has an [[inverse function]] ''G''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''k<sup>N</sup>''&nbsp;→&nbsp;''k<sup>N</sup>'' that is also regular.
| {{partial|{{sort|1|}}For <math>N = 3</math>, a counterexample was given by [[Levent Alpöge]], who claimed using a [[large language model]] assistance.<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=__alpoge__ |number=2079028340955197566 |title=hello there the jacobian conjecture is false}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/2580374-ais-solution-to-87-year-old-riddle-takes-mathematicians-by-surprise/|title=AI's solution to 87-year-old riddle takes mathematicians by surprise|author= Matthew Sparkes|date=July 20, 2026|publisher=[[New Scientist]]}}</ref>}} This counterexample induces counterexamples for <math>N \geq 4</math>.

It is unsure if this problem should be thought as resolved completely, since the case <math>N = 2</math> remains open,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bisi|first1=Elia|last2=Dyszewski|first2=Piotr|last3=Gantert|first3=Nina|last4=Johnston |first4=Samuel G. G.|last5=Prochno |first5=Joscha |last6=Schmid |first6=Dominik |title=Random planar trees and the Jacobian conjecture |journal=Journal of the London Mathematical Society |volume=113 |issue=1 |year=2026 |article-number=e70416 |doi=10.1112/jlms.70416 |quote=The Jacobian conjecture ... is one of the outstanding open problems in all of mathematics ... even the case n=2 is still open.
|arxiv=2301.08221 }}</ref> with specialist literature distinguishing its status from the case <math>N\ge 3</math>.<ref name="VandenEssen1997">{{cite journal |last=van den Essen |first=Arno |title=To Believe or Not to Believe: The Jacobian Conjecture |journal=Rendiconti del Seminario Matematico della Università e Politecnico di Torino |volume=55 |issue=4 |year=1997 |at=p. 287 |url=https://seminariomatematico.polito.it/rendiconti/cartaceo/55-4/283.pdf
 |quote=For n = 2 the conjecture might be true, however ... there is an enormous difference between <math>n = 2</math> and <math>n\geq  3</math>!
}}</ref><ref name="Formanek2011">{{cite journal |last=Formanek |first=Edward |title=Theorems of W. W. Stothers and the Jacobian Conjecture in two variables |journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society |volume=139 |issue=4 |year=2011  |at=p. 1140 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-2010-10523-3 |quote=There is strong evidence for the two-variable Jacobian Conjecture, but not for the n-variable conjecture.
|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Borisov2014">{{cite journal |last=Borisov |first=Alexander |title=On two invariants of divisorial valuations at infinity |journal=Journal of Algebraic Combinatorics |volume=39 |issue=3 |year=2014 |at=p. 692 |doi=10.1007/s10801-013-0462-9 |quote=The two-dimensional case has been especially well studied, but is still wide open.

}}</ref><ref name="MohJacobian">{{cite web |last=Moh |first=T. T. |title=Jacobian Conjecture |website=Department of Mathematics, Purdue University |url=https://www.math.purdue.edu/~ttm/jacobian.html |access-date=20 July 2026 |quote=Certainly there are even harder Jacobian conjectures for three or more variables. | 17th
| Solving [[polynomial equation]]s in [[polynomial time]] in the average case
| {{yes|{{sort|1|}}Resolved. C. Beltrán and L. M. Pardo found two uniform probabilistic algorithms (average [[Las Vegas algorithm]]) for this problem<ref>{{cite journal | first1 = Carlos | last1 = Beltrán | first2 = Luis Miguel | last2 = Pardo |title= On Smale's 17th Problem: A Probabilistic Positive answer |journal=Foundations of Computational Mathematics |volume=8 |issue=1 |year=2008 |pages=1–43 |doi=10.1007/s10208-005-0211-0 |url=http://personales.unican.es/beltranc/archivos/Smale17FoCM.pdf| s2cid = 11528635 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | first1 = Carlos | last1 = Beltrán | first2 = Luis Miguel | last2 = Pardo |title= Smale's 17th Problem: Average Polynomial Time to compute affine and projective solutions|journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society|volume=22 | issue = 2 |year=2009 |pages=363–385|url=http://personales.unican.es/beltranc/archivos/AffSmale17JAMS.pdf |doi=10.1090/s0894-0347-08-00630-9|bibcode=2009JAMS...22..363B|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | first1 = Carlos | last1 = Beltrán | first2 = Luis Miguel | last2 = Pardo |title=Fast Linear Homotopy to Find Approximate Zeros of Polynomial Systems |journal=Foundations of Computational Mathematics |volume=11 |issue=1 |year=2011 |pages=95–129 |doi=10.1007/s10208-010-9078-9 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10208-010-9078-9|url-access=subscription }}</ref>  <br /><br />[[Felipe Cucker|F. Cucker]] and [[Peter Bürgisser|P. Bürgisser]] made the [[smoothed analysis]] of a probabilistic algorithm ''à la Beltrán-Pardo'' and then exhibited a deterministic algorithm running in time <math>N^{O(\log\log N)}</math>.<ref>{{cite journal | first1 = Felipe | last1 = Cucker | first2 = Peter | last2 = Bürgisser |title= On a problem posed by Steve Smale|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=174 |issue=3|year=2011 |doi=10.4007/annals.2011.174.3.8 |pages=1785–1836|arxiv=0909.2114 | s2cid = 706015 }}</ref><br /><br />Finally, [[Pierre Lairez|P. Lairez]] found an alternative method to de-randomize the algorithm ''à la Beltrán-Pardo'' and thus found a deterministic algorithm which runs in average polynomial time.<ref>{{cite journal | first1 = Pierre | last1 = Lairez |title= A deterministic algorithm to compute approximate roots of polynomial systems in polynomial average time |journal=Foundations of Computational Mathematics |volume=to appear |year=2016 | issue = 5 | pages = 1265–1292 | doi = 10.1007/s10208-016-9319-7 | arxiv = 1507.05485 | s2cid = 8333924 }}</ref><br /><br />All these works follow Shub and Smale's foundational work (the "Bezout series") started in <ref>{{cite journal | first1 = Michael | last1 = Shub | first2 = Stephen | last2 = Smale |title= Complexity of Bézout's theorem. I. Geometric aspects |journal=J. Amer. Math. Soc. |volume=6 |issue=2 |year=1993 |pages=459–501 |doi=10.2307/2152805| jstor = 2152805 }}.</ref>}}
| 2008–2016
